Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Send Additions/Suggestions to: sjoh...@math.scarolina.edu:
If you wish to add your support for any of the suggestions,
send mail as well.

Please include "house rule" in the subject line.

House Rules
===========

General Rules
-------------
o. The (D) symbol has no affect on the game. All actions targetting another

Methuselah or her cards directly are directed. All other actions are not.
Thus, (D) bleed cards can still only target your Prey, as per the rules.
Note that this does not affect votes in any way.
[LSJ]

o. Reaction cards can be played by Minion controlled by a Methuselah

other than the Methuselah controlling the action minion, even on
your own turn.
[LSJ]

o. Master Out-of-Turn cards may be played whenever appropriate in lieu
of you next Master Phase, as per the rulebook.
[LSJ]

o. Actions by vampires in torpor can be blocked by Kindred ONLY.
[LSJ]

o. Transferring equipment from a vampire in torpor can be done by
Kindred ONLY.
[LSJ]

o. Combat cannot occur with a vampire in torpor. Diablerie is possible
if the opposing minion is a ready vampire, otherwise nothing happens.
[LSJ]

o. Cards which cannot be used by vampires going to torpor (Pulled Fangs,
Amaranth) cannot be used by a vampire burned in combat either.
[LSJ]

o. Strike: Combat Ends resolves during normal strike resolution (still
before first strikes). If the opposing strike is also: End Combat,
both have their usual effect.
[LSJ]

Card-Specific Rules
-------------------
Blood Rage - requires (th) not (fo).
[LSJ]

Bonding - only one of Bonding, Condition, or Threats Card may be used
during a single action.
[LSJ]

Brujah Frenzy - may be played only on a Ready Brujah. Can only send the
Acting Brujah into combat with a Ready Minion.
[LSJ]

Chainsaw - does 3 damage each strike, not usable first round.
[LSJ]

Chantry - may be applied during Untap, not Master phase.
[LSJ]

Charming Lobby - use as an action to call a vote at +1 stealth. If
successful, call a vote by playing a Political Action card or by naming
a vote allowed by a card in play. If the vote succeeds, the next vote
will pass as well.
[LSJ]

Concealed Weapon - does not require (ob).
[LSJ]

Conditioning - see Bonding.
[LSJ]

Day Operation - is unblockable, even with the aid of Eagle's Sight.
[LSJ]

Eagle's Sight - allows only the attempt to block. Attempting to block an
unblockable action is futile.
[LSJ]

Elder Kindred Network - has no effect on a successful Referendum.
[LSJ]

Enchant Kindred - is at +1 stealth when attempting the superior version.
[LSJ]

Faceless Night - taps any minion who attempted to block when the action
becomes blocked or when the action resolves, as appropriate.
[LSJ]

Frenzy - may be played even if you have not Minions involved in the Combat.
[LSJ]

Haven Uncovered - does not prevent its victim from being attacked in torpor.
[LSJ]

Lextalionis - may be called when a Methuselah has gained a victory point
since the start (untap) of your last turn.
[LSJ]

Monacle of Clarity - may not refer to future questions, answers, statements,
nor commands. If it invokes a relationship (p -> q), then the answerer is
free to make p true without regard to her ability to make the relationship
agree with her answer. Once p is true, the answerer becomes bound to make
the relationship agree with her answer, if possible.
[LSJ]

Parity Shift - may only redistribute pool up to the difference between the
selected Methuselah's pool and your own pool.
[LSJ]

Rotshreck - must target a vampire actually targetted by an act which would
cause aggravated damage. If the act is unperformed (due to Combat Ends or
steal/destroy equipment with first strike, e.g.), Rotshreck may not be
used. This does not apply if the damage is foiled (by dodge, fortitude,
Merril Molitor, Blood Rage/Fury, e.g.)
[LSJ]

Sport Bike - is not optional.
[LSJ]

Taste of Vitae - only one of these may be played per minion per round.
[LSJ]

The 2nd Tradition - may be used by an untapped Prince/Justicar for +2
intercept.
[LSJ]

---------------------
[LSJ] - L. Scott Johnson (sjoh...@math.scarolina.edu)
Threats - see Bonding.

Sigh. You'll notice that I changed the subject line above. If
you're going to call this net.personality generated, this rule does not
belong. We have *no* consensus on this rule, and thus either no
interpretation of this rule should be provided or both interpretations
should be provided. If you provide one side of something that is still
in debate, you are providing your own personal house rules, not the
net's house rules.

>o. Reaction cards can be played by Minion controlled by a Methuselah
> other than the Methuselah controlling the action minion, even on
> your own turn.
> [LSJ]

The only time this ever is broken is during the Madness Network.
Personally, I think an erratum on the MMN is much more appropriate than
a problematic change to a metarule.

>o. Combat cannot occur with a vampire in torpor. Diablerie is possible
> if the opposing minion is a ready vampire, otherwise nothing happens.
> [LSJ]

get into combat in the current rules?

Well, here's one ruling that probably will get net.approval...

>Bonding - only one of Bonding, Condition, or Threats Card may be used
> during a single action.
> [LSJ]

I would word it so that 'card' was up front and hard to miss
rather than stuck back behind. Even better is to just remove the
awkward wording completely and word the cards like so:
"Only one action modifier may be used to increase the bleed of a
single action after it is announced." This says in effect the same
thing (since all of the modifiers are B/C/T) much more cleanly, and
allows for future cards. Should they *want* future cards to be able to
add yet more bleed, that specific card could make itself an exception.

>Chainsaw - does 3 damage each strike, not usable first round.
> [LSJ]

We play it with the Chainsaw strikes as written, but add the
word "Melee" to the card.

>Chantry - may be applied during Untap, not Master phase.
> [LSJ]

>Elder Kindred Network - has no effect on a successful Referendum.

binding command device. Please use it with that intent. If your play
group is unable to do so, do not play with it."

>Parity Shift - may only redistribute pool up to the difference between the
> selected Methuselah's pool and your own pool.
> [LSJ]

Again, still in dispute, and thus shouldn't be here.

> cause aggravated damage. If the act is unperformed (due to Combat Ends or

> used. This does not apply if the damage is foiled (by dodge, fortitude,
> Merril Molitor, Blood Rage/Fury, e.g.)
> [LSJ]

It still takes a minute to figure out that you're saying that it
hoses the vampire about to receive the damage. That needs to be crystal
clear from word one, especially given the previous debate on the card.
The rest can be a separate paragraph and nobody would care.

>Sport Bike - is not optional.
> [LSJ]

Woah! Where did that one come from? If anything, that one will
shortly be in dispute, because Equipment is not mandatory. Why should
the Bike be mandatory when all other equipment isn't?

>The 2nd Tradition - may be used by an untapped Prince/Justicar for +2
> intercept.
> [LSJ]

The card should read "Prince/Justicar. +2 Intercept. If
tapped, vampire untaps. Vampire must attempt to block."

apologies, joseph, but i'm siding with l. scott on this one -- a
comprehensive rules framework allows rule-breaking cards to function
smoothly, whereas multiply errata'd/liquid paper'd/band-aided rules on
each and every individual card simply create poor gameflow (if you don't
have access to the errata list, how do you play?) and leave the door open
for further rulebreaking cards that have to be further errata'd.

also, since movement of the slow body and rapid healing (the two action
cards that currently allow action in torpor, as far as i know) specifically
mention that if blocked, there is no combat, et. al., it seems natural
to make it a global rule, which would fix brujah frenzy without requiring
errata, as well as taking care of any future cards that permit action in
torpor without having to deal with them on a case-by-case basis.

reaction cards (and, imo, it should have said so on the card), and that
that effect is part of its unpleasantness. that's a ruling i can live
with, and it renders the current madness network discussion moot.

a m:tg analogy: dwarven weaponsmith, in antiquities and revised. the anti-
quities version had a large block of small print defining its use, text
that was open to loopholing and misinterpretation. in revised, 'sacrifice'
was clearly defined, became a global rule, and the cardtext of the revised
weaponsmith was modified to use this new definition. an elegant solution
to a card that went outside current rules.

: no combat occurs, but the blocking vamp gets the opportunity to
: diablerize.

This is an example of a broken card and/or a broken rule. We have a
situation where two things are supposed to be happening simultaneously,
both perfectly legal according to part of the rules and illegal according
to others.

The Brujah rescues itself from torpor, successfully, then has a BF played
on it. It must go into combat, and cannot go into combat simultaneously.

In effect, you _have_ to have a house rule to cover this situation,
because the existing rules do not cover it. I am of the opinion that the
action is simply blocked (as it says on the card), and whoever is
designated as the recipient of a frenzying Brujah now has the opportunity
to attempt diablerie. No combat occurs, and it diablerie is not chosen,
then the Brujah slips back into Torpor, minus 2 blood for the attempt.

In other words, I like the 'no combat coming out of torpor' part of the
rules better than the actual text of the card...

All this hooha results from trying to shoehorn all retainers into one
ruling. From the game standpoint, some retainers are written to be
optional (Ghoul Retainer, Resplendent Protecter, Jackie Therman), while
others are written to be mandatory (Charnas, Wolf Companion, Murder of
Crows). From the simulation standpoint, some retainers can and will do
the vampire's bidding (the human ones), while others either can't
understand the bidding (Wolves and Crows) or don't care (Charnas).

I find it telling that there appears to be a perfect match between the
game and the simulation standpoints - the retainers the vampire couldn't
give orders to are written as mandatory, those it could give orders to are
written as optional.

The out-of-combat retainers (Taisha Morgan, Mr. Winthrop, etc.) require a
ruling. From the game standpoint, they are equivalent to certain
equipment and ought to work by the same rules. At present, there is no
method for declaring when an out-of-combat retainer or equipment is used,
so they all should be mandatory. Logically, the equipment can simply not
be turned on, and most of the the relevant retainers are clearly able to
understand "take the day off" (Raven Spy is the exception). I would be
happy with a ruling on when those abilities get used, making them all
optional. I would be content to leave things as they are, with all these
abilities mandatory because there's no rules for saying whether you use
them. But splitting them just because of a compulsion to issue blanket
rules where they are neither necessary nor appropriate? I can't sign on
to that.

Curt Adams (curt...@aol.com)

Remember that each player's turn does not cover a single day. If you want
to argue whether the ruling is reasonable from a simulation standpoint, I
would point out that each turn is probably weeks or months worth of time,
not a couple of days, and it's extremely strange that you would tell
Tasha to go away for these two months, come back for these two, go away

ditch a combat-oriented retainer for a day or two, since combats would
only cover that kind of timeframe, but there isn't a compelling argument
for bleed retainers (for example) just "taking the month off".
